The '''2011–12 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team''' represented [[Vanderbilt University]] during the [[2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Commodores, members of the [[Southeastern Conference]], were coached by [[Kevin Stallings]], and celebrated their 60th season in their current home arena, [[Memorial Gymnasium (Vanderbilt University)|Memorial Gymnasium]]. After a 21–10 regular season that fell short of lofty preseason expectations, the Commodores captured their first SEC Tournament Championship in 61 seasons on March 11, 2012, by defeating [[2011–12 Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball team|Georgia]], [[2011–12 Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball team|Ole Miss]], and top-ranked [[2011–12 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] in consecutive days.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=320710096 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120315051901/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=320710096 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 15, 2012 |title=Vanderbilt ends Kentucky's 24-game win streak to win SEC tournament |date=March 11, 2012 |accessdate=March 11, 2012}}</ref> In the [[2012 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2012 NCAA tournament]] they defeated [[2011–12 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team|Harvard]] in the second round before falling in the third round to [[2011–12 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] to finish the season 25–11.

==Before the season==
The Commodores came off a [[2010–11 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|2010–11 season]] that ended with a second-round (first game) upset by [[2010–11 Richmond Spiders men's basketball team|Richmond]] in the [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. This continued a recent history of tournament disappointments for Vanderbilt, whose last three NCAA appearances had all ended with a first-game loss to a double-digit seed.<ref name=Katz>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/blog/_/name/katz_andy/id/6847643/festus-ezeli-continues-learn-game |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111011163910/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/blog/_/name/katz_andy/id/6847643/festus-ezeli-continues-learn-game |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 11, 2011 |title=Festus Ezeli continues to learn the game |first=Andy |last=Katz |authorlink=Andy Katz |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=August 9, 2011 |accessdate=August 15, 2011}}</ref>

During the offseason, the coaching staff saw one change when assistant [[King Rice]] was hired as head coach at [[Monmouth Hawks men's basketball|Monmouth]].<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.gomuhawks.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=62254&SPID=6806&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=14300&ATCLID=205126034 |title=Monmouth to Announce King Rice as New Head Men's Basketball Coach |publisher=Monmouth University Sports Information |date=April 1, 2011 <!--|accessdate=April 1, 2011--> |accessdate=August 19, 2011}}</ref> Rice was replaced by David Cason, a former player under Stallings at [[Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball|Illinois State]] who had spent the previous six seasons as an assistant with [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa]].<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://vucommodores.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041511aaa.html |title=David Cason named to Vanderbilt MBB staff |publisher=Vanderbilt University Sports Information |date=April 15, 2011 |accessdate=August 19, 2011}}</ref>

==2011–12 outlook==
In a major offseason development, three of the Commodores' most important players—[[Festus Ezeli]], [[John Jenkins (basketball)|John Jenkins]], and [[Jeffery Taylor]]—all spurned the [[2011 NBA Draft|NBA draft]] and announced they would return for the 2011–12 season.<ref name=Bergeron>{{cite web|url=https://insider.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story?id=6836994&_slug_=cbb-vanderbilt-commodores-2011-12-summer-buzz-preview&action=upsell&appRedirect=http%253a%252f%252finsider.espn.go.com%252fncb%252fstory%253fid%253d6836994%2526_slug_%253dcbb-vanderbilt-commodores-2011-12-summer-buzz-preview |title=CBB Summer Buzz: Vanderbilt |first=Elena |last=Bergeron |work=ESPN.com |date=August 9, 2011 |access-date=August 19, 2011}} (full article behind paywall; cited information in free preview)</ref><ref name="AP return">{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=6397537 |title=John Jenkins returning to Vanderbilt |author=Associated Press |work=ESPN.com |date=April 20, 2011 |access-date=August 19, 2011}}</ref> Jenkins, the SEC's leading scorer in 2010–11 at 19.5 points per game,<ref name="2011 SEC stats">{{cite web|url=http://www.secdigitalnetwork.com/Portals/3/SEC%20Website/menshoops/CONFLDRS.HTM#conf.wki |title=Individual Basketball Statistics |work=2010–11 SEC Men's Basketball Statistics |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=April 2, 2011 |accessdate=August 19, 2011}}</ref> was chosen for the All-SEC first team.<ref name="All-SEC 2011">{{cite press release|url=http://www.secdigitalnetwork.com/NEWS/tabid/473/Article/222025/2011-sec-mens-hoops-awards-announced.aspx |title=2011 SEC Men’s Hoops Awards Announced |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 8, 2011 |accessdate=August 19, 2011| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20110716030100/http://www.secdigitalnetwork.com/NEWS/tabid/473/Article/222025/2011-sec-mens-hoops-awards-announced.aspx| archivedate= 16 July 2011 | url-status= live}}</ref> Ezeli, who averaged 13 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 2.6 blocks<ref name="2011 SEC stats"/> in a breakout season, was named to the All-SEC second team,<ref name="All-SEC 2011"/> and was also named by multiple sources as one of the most improved players in the country.<ref name=Katz/><ref name=Torre>{{cite web|url= http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1182629/index.htm |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110304225533/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1182629/index.htm |url-status= dead |archive-date= March 4, 2011 |title=How Did I Get Here? |first=Pablo S. |last=Torre |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=March 7, 2011 |accessdate=August 19, 2011}}</ref> Taylor averaged 14.7 points<ref name="2011 SEC stats"/> while being named to the All-SEC second team, as well as the SEC All-Defensive Team.<ref name="All-SEC 2011"/> Ezeli, Jenkins, and Taylor were all named by ''Basketball Prospectus'' in its 2011–12 preseason outlook as among the top 20 players in college basketball, making Vanderbilt the only Division I men's team with three top-20 performers.<ref name=Bergeron/>

These decisions meant that Vanderbilt would return all five of its starters from last season, all of them seniors except for Jenkins, a junior.<ref name=Brennan>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/33847/summer-buzz-vanderbilt-commodores |title=Summer Buzz: Vanderbilt Commodores |first=Eamonn |last=Brennan |work=College Basketball Nation Blog |publisher=ESPN.com |date=August 9, 2011 |access-date=August 19, 2011}}</ref> Another returning starter, [[point guard]] [[Brad Tinsley]], led the SEC in assists in 2010–11 with 4.6 per game.<ref name=Bergeron/><ref name="2011 SEC stats"/>

The Commodores thus were widely projected as a preseason top-10 team,<ref name=Katz/><ref name=Bergeron/> with [[ESPN]]'s [[List of members of the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame#Contributors|Hall of Fame]] commentator [[Dick Vitale]] going so far as to rank them #5 in his preseason top 40.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/dickvitale/story/_/id/6787669/dick-vitale-preseason-top-10-unc-takes-top-spot |title=Dickie V Preseason Top 40: Top 10 |first=Dick |last=Vitale |authorlink=Dick Vitale |work=ESPN.com |date=July 26, 2011 |access-date=August 19, 2011}}</ref>

Less than a month before the start of the season, the NCAA suspended Ezeli 6 games after accepting a meal and hotel room from a Vanderbilt alumnus during a summer trip. He was able to practice with the team during the suspension, and was also eligible to play in the team's preseason exhibition game (but was unable to play in that game). Ezeli came off his suspension for the [[2011–12 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]] game on November 28;<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7116601/vanderbilt-commodores-center-festus-ezeli-suspended-first-six-games-season |title=Festus Ezeli suspended six games |author=Associated Press |work=ESPN.com |date=October 17, 2011 |access-date=October 28, 2011}}</ref> however, he suffered a sprained knee during a late-October practice,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=313150238 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111116054531/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=313150238 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 16, 2011 |title=No. 7 Vanderbilt 78, Oregon 64 |author=Associated Press |work=ESPN.com |date=November 11, 2011 |accessdate=November 12, 2011}}</ref> and did not return until the [[Davidson Wildcats men's basketball|Davidson]] game on December 7.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=313412166 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319171940/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=313412166 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 19, 2012 |title=Vanderbilt 87, Davidson 83 |author=Associated Press |work=ESPN.com |date=December 7, 2011 |accessdate=December 16, 2011}}</ref>
